sample_unit: independent simulation seeds per configuration (four dispatch policies, four operating scenarios)

links.outcome: DQN dispatch policy versus heuristic policies on peak occupancy and length of stay
links.effect: At +40% demand, DQN cut peak occupancy from 76.2 to 67.4 patients (-11.5%) with no length-of-stay penalty (98.31 vs 98.48 min; p = 0.878). At baseline load all policies were indistinguishable.
links.quote: Under baseline load, all four policies were statistically indistinguishable.

unlisted_practices: Shapley-value explainability layer giving audience-differentiated clinical and managerial narratives for dispatch recommendations
Critical in silico validation protocol using queueing-theory checks (Little's law) to expose instrumentation artifacts in the digital twin and equity metric
Bidirectional digital twin synchronization with stochastic scenario ensembles to run closed-loop prediction-decision-feedback

screen.reason: Evaluates a proposed cyber-physical system (digital twin simulation + deep reinforcement learning agent + XAI) for emergency department patient dispatching in silico, comparing it to standard heuristics rather than testing a specific deployment safeguard or organizational practice.
